narrative_purpose: Shows that the 'fixed' planet is not perfectly fixed: over one orbit Polyphemus traces a slow loop against the stars - drifting east-west and riding north-south - the libration that also lets us peer around the edges of our own Moon.
subject: The banded disc of Polyphemus shown as a cluster of slightly offset ghosted positions tracing a small lazy figure-eight or loop against a field of fixed stars, high above a dark low Pandoran ridge. The central, most solid position is the planet; the fainter offset repeats suggest its slow nod east, west, high and low.
scene: Night-into-twilight sky over a dark forested horizon, the planet large and high, a quiet starfield behind it, the faint looping repeats reading as motion over time.
camera: Wide upward view from a dark ridge, planet high in the frame, horizon low.
light: Cool indigo night sky, faint reflected glow on the planet's near face, a dim bioluminescent rim along the dark ridge below; the ghosted repeats slightly fainter than the main disc.
palette: Void-indigo sky, cream-rust planet bands, faint teal horizon glow, pale star dusting.
style: Painterly naturalist astronomical plate, soft, atmospheric, NOT a render and NOT a hard vector diagram.
detail_level: Moderate: main planet crisp, the offset repeats softer to read as a slow loop of motion; ridge low-detail and dark.
composition: Planet and its small looping trail of ghosted positions centred high, generous starfield, low dark horizon along the bottom for grounding.
consistency_notes: Same Polyphemus as the cover (identical bands and eye-storm). The looping repeats must read as the same planet at slightly different sky positions, not as several different planets. No drawn motion lines or arrows.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no drawn path lines, no grid, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
